evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-10-31"} returned 201 with dueDate "2026-10-31". I created other todos with dates (2026-11-01, 2027-01-01, 2020-01-01), and all came back as plain calendar dates. POST /todos with {"title":"nodue"} returned 201 with dueDate null, so the date is optional.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/3 {"dueDate":"2026-01-01"} returned 200 and changed the date from 2027-01-01 to 2026-01-01. PATCH {"title":"future2"} left the date unchanged. PATCH {"dueDate":null} returned 200 with dueDate null, so the date was removed.
evidence.AC3: POST with dueDate "2026-02-30", "31-12-2026", "abc" and "2026-13-01" each returned 400 with the error 'dueDate must be a YYYY-MM-DD date'. POST with dueDate 123 returned 400. PATCH /todos/1 {"dueDate":"2026-02-30"} returned 400.
evidence.AC4: Today in UTC is 2026-11-01. I had todos with dates yesterday, today, 2027-01-01 and 2020-01-01 (this last one marked done), plus one with no date and one whose date I removed. GET /todos?overdue=true returned only the todo dated 2026-10-31. Excluded: due today, done with a past date, no date, and date removed. In the full GET /todos list, only the 2026-10-31 todo has overdue true.
evidence.AC5: The list page at / showed 2026-10-31 next to 'past', 2026-11-01 next to 'today' and 2020-01-01 next to 'pastdone'. The todos with no date showed none.
evidence.AC6: In the page snapshot, only the 'past' todo (2026-10-31) showed the text 'überfällig'. The todos due today, done with a past date, with no date and with the date removed showed no label.
evidence.AC7: The page has a checkbox labelled 'nur überfällige'. Clicking it reduced the list to a single item, 'past' with the 'überfällig' label.
